CONFIRMED PINNED QUIRK (the probe first expected pruning and the run disproved it): the startup verify (server-main.js:304 -> DiskCache.verify) passes the hashed cache FILENAME back to node-persist removeItem as a storage key, and node-persist hashes it again (local-storage.js getDatumPath -> sha256(key)), so the removal targets sha256(hashedFilename), which does not exist. Ordinary stale records — a deleted card's records, an old mtime key — therefore SURVIVE the startup verify; only a record whose key literally equals its own hashed filename is removed. Observed here: deletedRecordGone=false and everyRemainingRecordIsACurrentCardKey=false with both records still on disk. The pinned fixture tests/oracle/sillytavern-1.19.0-character-disk-cache.json records the same behaviour (jpg/stale retained, "shadow" removed), and internal/startup/character_disk_cache.go reproduces it deliberately.

CONFIRMED from the real run: a broken cache path cannot break character reads; the failure is caught and logged (characters.js:193-195, 204-206). The row records what happened, including the enotdir/eisdir wording that was actually logged.
rows.setup: the probe replaced <DATA_ROOT>/_cache/characters with a regular file, before this process read any card

rows.classification: OBSERVED: after the directory was restored, the process's already-created store instance stayed broken (the earlier instance() failed on the file), so the read served the card but no record was rewritten in this process; a NEW process starts a fresh instance (C15/C16). Recorded, not assumed.
CONFIRMED: with performance.useDiskCache=false the cache directory is not created by startup and no record is written by a read; the read still succeeds

OBSERVED from the real run: GoTavern reads the same data root without corrupting the pinned cache records, and the pinned server serves the card again afterwards. Whether the Go side PRUNES exactly like pinned is covered by internal/startup/character_disk_cache_test.go; this row records the hand-over state.

unproven: The 5-minute in-process verify interval is NOT triggered by waiting 5 minutes here; the observed pruning point in this probe is the STARTUP verify (C12), and even that is the pinned misaddressed-key quirk, not a real prune.
Memory-cache EVICTION under the 100 MB capacity is not exercised.
Node->Go->Node proves the pinned records survive a Go boot, not that Go and pinned prune byte-identically; the Go fixture test owns that comparison.

C15: no directory, no record, reads still work
